front: What is the unit of electric field?
back: N/C or V/m. E = F/q.
Pair of equal and opposite charges +q and −q separated by distance 2a.
p = q × 2a. Directed from −q to +q. SI unit: C·m.

front: Torque on dipole in uniform field
back: τ = p × E. Maximum when θ = 90°. Minimum (zero) when θ = 0°.

front: Torque on dipole when p ⊥ E vs p ∥ E
back:
τ ⊥ E: τ = pE (maximum)
τ ∥ E: τ = 0 (minimum)

front: How does dipole field fall with distance?
back: As 1/r³. Falls faster than point charge field (1/r²).
∮E·dA = q_enclosed/ε₀. Total flux = enclosed charge ÷ ε₀.
Φ = EAcosθ. Maximum when field ⊥ surface (θ = 0°).

front: Field inside uniformly charged spherical shell
back: Zero. By Gauss's Law: Gaussian surface inside encloses no charge.

front: E due to infinite plane sheet of charge
back: E = σ/(2ε₀). Independent of distance from sheet.

front: E due to uniformly charged thin wire at distance r
back: E = λ/(2πε₀r). Falls as 1/r.

front: Why do electric field lines never cross?
back: Field at any point has a unique direction. Crossing lines would imply two directions — physically impossible.

Conductors: free charge carriers → charges flow.
Insulators: no free carriers → charges don't flow.
Charging by redistribution of charges without contact. A nearby charged object causes charge separation.
Net force on a charge = vector sum of forces due to all other charges individually.
Experiences BOTH torque AND net force (unlike uniform field where net force = 0).

front: Relative strength of electric vs gravitational force
back: Electric force is ~10³⁹ times stronger than gravity between proton and electron.
Total charge of an isolated system remains constant. Charge can transfer but total is conserved.
Total charge of system = algebraic sum of individual charges. Q = q₁ + q₂ + ...

front: Why does a neutral conductor get attracted to a charged object?
back: Charged object induces opposite charge on the near side. Non-uniform field exerts net attractive force.

front: Electric field due to spherical shell — outside
back: E = q/(4πε₀r²). Same as point charge at centre.

front: Force between two charges when distance is doubled
back: Force becomes one-fourth (1/4) of original value. F ∝ 1/r².
